metadata.title: Persisting Progress Across Context Windows
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: how does an agent with 200 features to implement know to resume at feature 51 instead of replaying the first 50 when its context window resets? Lands the carry-out that the context window is a workspace, not memory — the file plus git is the memory.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B04 (feature 51, the first-incomplete lookup across the session boundary)

beats.narration_text: People assume an agent remembers where it left off. It doesn't — context resets each session. It checks a file instead. How does it know to resume at feature 51, not feature 1?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'An agent with 200 features just remembers where it left off. How does it resume at feature 51, not feature 1?', hesitates on 'remembers', corrects to 'checks'

props.text:
An agent with 200 features
just remembers where it left off.
How does it resume at feature 51,
not feature 1?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('remembers' -> 'checks') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: A context window has a limit. When it fills, the session ends. The next session starts blank — no memory of what passed or failed. The agent has two options: re-read everything, which burns half the new context, or guess. Neither works.

shot.new_visual_element: A filled 'Session 1' bar next to an empty 'Session 2' bar, two dim arrows branching to 'RE-READ EVERYTHING' and 'GUESS', both struck

production_viz.label: Two bad options
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a filled bar labeled 'SESSION 1 — context full'. A vertical divider labeled 'session boundary'. Right: an empty bar labeled 'SESSION 2 — blank'. Two arrows branch from it toward 'RE-READ EVERYTHING' (dim, costly) and 'GUESS' (crimson, struck through).

beats.narration_text: The fix is one file: feature_list.json, 200 entries, each with an id and a status — incomplete or passing. Git commits one per feature, an immutable ledger. Say session one finishes features 1 through 50 — each flips to passing, each committed. Feature 51 is the first one still marked incomplete.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — a vertical list of 200 rows; rows 1-50 flip from incomplete to passing during session 1; row 51 stays lit as 'first incomplete'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — feature 51, first incomplete
production_viz.mechanic: A tall vertical list of numbered rows on cream, status badges reading 'incomplete' (INK) or 'passing' (teal check). Rows 1-50 flip to passing in sequence under a 'SESSION 1' label, each accompanied by a small git-commit tick. Row 51 stays on 'incomplete', ringed in crimson with the label 'first incomplete'. THIS EXACT LIST COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B04.

beats.narration_text: Every new session does the same three things: open feature_list.json, find the first entry still marked incomplete, and start there. Implement it, run the tests, commit, mark it passing. Then repeat — read, find the gap, fill it.

shot.new_visual_element: Four-step loop diagram: OPEN FILE -> FIND FIRST INCOMPLETE -> IMPLEMENT + TEST + COMMIT -> MARK PASSING, looping back

production_viz.label: The loop
production_viz.mechanic: Four boxes in a cycle, connected by arrows: 'OPEN feature_list.json' -> 'FIND FIRST INCOMPLETE' -> 'IMPLEMENT + TEST + COMMIT' -> 'MARK PASSING', with the last arrow curving back to the first box.

beats.narration_text: Session two opens the same file. It finds feature 51 marked incomplete — the same one session one left behind — and starts exactly there. No re-reading the first fifty, no guessing. By the end of session two, features 51 through 100 are passing too.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same 200-row list as B02; row 51 highlighted as where session 2 resumes; rows 51-100 flip to passing

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — session 2 resumes at 51
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 LIST COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical. Row 51 (still ringed crimson from B02) is where a 'SESSION 2' label enters and starts reading. Rows 51-100 flip to passing in sequence with commit ticks, mirroring B02's animation exactly. No motion touches rows 1-50.

beats.narration_text: An agent's context window isn't its memory — it's a workspace. Externalize the state to a file plus git, and each new session just reads it, finds the first gap, and fills it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Externalize my agent's progress to a feature_list.json plus git, so it can resume across sessions — then prove it picks up exactly where it left off, without replaying finished work. Liam, in for Bear.
